questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A strong student-body along with good courses available.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - The university is very informative upon arrival and very helpful in case of needing further assistance

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was multiple seminars where we were introduced to a number of people to contact in case we needed help or information, along with plenty resources on how to get settled abroad, what was required and recommended.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very limited options. Basically one day before semester start (couple of months before) registration for housing through the university is opened, and if you are not ready (and mostly willing to take anything that isn't taken already) you wont get housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There were multiple restaurants that offered deals to students. For grocerystores there werent any nearby (affordable that is), so one had to bike for 15-20 minutes for the nearest grocery store. The most common one does not take credit-card, so getting a dutch bank account is vital. 

For the dorms we were staying at, no kitchen utensils were supplied, so most (if not all) had to go buy brand new kitchen utensils (even cutlery, dishes and glasses) on moving-in day. Otherwise the kitchen equipment was basic. A kettle, a stovetop and a microwave.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Kitchen utensils does not come with the housing accomodation. The rooms are sparse but acceptable. Theres a lot of different dorms on campus, and it could be advantageous to research them beforehand. Especially "cambridgelaan" is not a nice dorm (housing wise) and if possible should be avoided.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After admittance through erasmus+, you are given an email on the UU portal. Through this you gain acces to most of the registration sites, although they themselves enlist you in your selected courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Plenty - service desks, open hours, different emails for different problems. Easy to find, as long as you know what your problem is.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was done for me before I arrived by the host institution

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Their portal for courses is quite confusing an often not up to date or plainly in dutch. There is a ton of options, but I would recommend setting up a phonecall or digital meeting with someone to guide you through what might be available to you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one entry-level class that was a lot of reading, but otherwise quite simple. Three "informatica" courses with a very high expectation and complex curriculum. The courses are seldom "easy" and require more time than I initially expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less mathematical, more practical, and a steep learning curve.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cognition and emotion
Image processing
Concurrency and Parallelism
Language and Compilers

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Concurrency and Parallelism
Language and Compilers
- These were the most instructive and constructive courses I had. They are very technical, so a student should have a interest in the complex workings of computers and machines.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Although it is recommended beforehand, getting a dutch bank account and transfering money around was quite the hassle, and cost a bit if done haphassardly.
Kitchen utensils - had to buy everything. Pots and pans, cutlery, knives, plates, cups, cutting-board ect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was quite costly unless you went out of your way to find a "jumbo" instead of a "albert heijn"

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a great sport center on campus named "olympos" that is affordable and offers all kinds of athletic and social activities. BuddyGoDutch was available for a great many social experiences and meeting exchange students and dutchies alike.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BuddyGoDutch

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the different cities of the netherlands. Den Haag, Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Leiden. Even belgium with Ghent, Brussels, Antwerp ect. There are beautiful forests, long lovely beaches and every city has its own feel and plenty to explore. There is a thing called "free walking tour" that is available in every city and I would strongly recommend it. No place in the netherlands is more than 1.5-2 hours by train from Utrecht.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The dutch people are very much like danes. Theres a exciting vibe amongst the exchange students, but I think anyone going on exchange are in part also looking for / enjoying that vibe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again - BuddyGoDutch, and meeting people in bars and parks

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Young dutch people are very loud. And self-centered at first glance, it is therefore important that you don't judge them harsly on first impressions

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlyness and light-hearted conversation - even with complete strangers

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Utilize buddy go dutch
Travel on weekends
Study from 9-17 in week-days, that should be plenty to follow the courses, and it leaves a lot of spare-time to enjoy socializing and day-travels

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The grading system is quite strange. Theres a narrow range from "passed" to "best in class" that is difficult to decipher. Talk to a dutch student about it, as to get a grasp on it - then it wont seem so scary.
Get (if possible) student housing through UU/SSH, having roommates and an extended social circle is crucial

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the places we travelled.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with the level of the courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
